questions.question: Bank rate is the rate at which:

options.text: Central Bank borrows loan from Government
Commercial banks lend loan to Central bank
Commercial banks lend loan to Government
Central bank lends loan to commercial banks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Central Bank lends loan to commercial banks.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Bank rate:

 
 
• Bank rate is a rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides the loan to commercial banks without keeping any security.
 
• There is no agreement on repurchase that will be drawn up or agreed upon with no collateral as well.
 
• The RBI allows short-term loans with the presence of collateral.
 
• This is known as Repo Rate.
 
• Bank Rates in India is determined by the RBI.
 
• It is usually higher than a Repo Rate on account of its ability to regulate liquidity.
 
• The current Bank Rate is 4.25%.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Monetary Policy:

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (RBI Act) was amended by the Finance Act, 2016, to provide for a statutory and institutionalized framework for a Monetary Policy Committee, for maintaining price stability, while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• The Monetary Policy Committee is entrusted with the task of fixing the benchmark policy rate (repo rate) required to contain inflation within the specified target level.
 
• The Government of India, in consultation with RBI, notified the ‘Inflation Target’ in the Gazette of India dated 5 August 2016 for the period beginning from the date of publication of the notification and ending on March 31, 2021, as 4%.
 
• At the same time, lower and upper tolerance levels were notified to be 2% and 6% respectively.
 
 
 
• Instruments of monetary policy:
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):
 
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio is a specified amount of bank deposits which banks are required to keep with the RBI in the form of reserves or balances.
 
• The higher the CRR with the RBI, the lower will be the liquidity in the system and vice versa.
 
• The CRR was reduced from 15% in 1990 to 5 % in 2002.
 
• The current CRR is 3.00%.
 
 
 
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):
 
 
• All financial institutions have to maintain a certain quantity of liquid assets with themselves at any point in time of their total time and demand liabilities.
 
• This is known as the Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
 
• The assets are kept in non-cash forms such as precious metals, bonds, etc.
 
• The current percentage of SLR is 18%.
 
 
 
• Bank Rate Policy:
 
 
• Also known as the discount rate, bank rates are interest charged by the RBI for providing funds and loans to the banking system.
 
• An increase in bank rate increases the cost of borrowing by commercial banks which results in the reduction in credit volume to the banks and hence the supply of money declines.
 
• An increase in the bank rate is the symbol of the tightening of the RBI monetary policy.
 
• The current Bank Rate is 4.25%.

questions.question: The term Stumping is related to which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Stumping is a term used in cricket when the wicket-keeper catches the ball and removes the bails before the batsman can return to the crease.
 
• It is a common way of dismissing batsmen in cricket.
 
• Stumps
 
 
• Three vertical posts serve as the stumps and hold up two bails. At each end of the pitch, a wicket is created by the combination of the stumps and bails, which are typically constructed of wood, most frequently ash.
 
• Each stump is identified with a unique name:
 
 
• Off stump is the stump that is on the other side of the wicket from the batsman.
 
• The middle of the three stumps is referred to as the middle stump.
 
• The leg stump is the stump that is on the same side as the batsman's legs as the wicket.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In baseball, a similar term is used called "tagging out" where a fielder touches the base with the ball before the runner reaches it.
 
• In tennis, stumping has no relevance as it is an individual sport and there is no wicket-keeper involved.-Basketball also has no relation to stumping as there are no wickets or bails involved in the game.

questions.question: Which term did Robert Hooke coin when he observed slices of cork, under a simple magnifying device?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Cell.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cell was discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665 by observing a piece of cork under a microscope.
 
• In his observation, he saw tiny boxlike cavities termed Cells.
 
• He described his detailed observation in his book Micrographia as an exploration of a tiny unseen world.
 
• His discovery opened a new dimension of knowledge and exploration to the smallest unit of life The Cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
 
• After Robert Hooke a dutch scientist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek discoverd other hidden microorganisms Bacteria and Protozoa.
 
• The classical cell theory was given by Theodor Schwann in 1839 and had three parts.
 
 
• ​All living organisms are made up of cells.
 
• Cells are basic units of life.
 
• Cells come from pre-existing cells

questions.question: Which of the following folk-dance forms is NOT predominantly performed in the Indian state of Maharashtra?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Rouff is NOT predominantly performed in the Indian state of Maharashtra.**
 
• **Tamasha** is a traditional form of** Marathi theatre** which includes music, dance, and drama.
 
• **Lavani **is a popular folk dance form in** Maharashtra** that involves a combination of song and dance.
 
• **Koli **is a traditional folk dance form performed by the** fisherfolk community in Maharashtra.**
 
• ** Folk dances** play an important role in preserving the cultural heritage of a region and are often **performed during festivals and celebrations.**

• Tamasha is believed to have originated in the 16th century and is known for its colorful costumes and lively music.
 
• Lavani is often performed by female dancers and is characterized by its fast-paced rhythm and suggestive lyrics.
 
• Koli is performed by both men and women and is accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the dholki and tasha.

questions.question: Industrial development is a precondition for _________ of unemployment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eradication.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Industrial development refers to the growth and expansion of industries in a country or region.
 
• ** Eradication of unemployment means the complete elimination of joblessness from the economy.**
 
• Industrial development is considered a precondition for eradicating unemployment because it creates new job opportunities and increases the demand for labor. 
 
• With the growth of industries, more people get employed in various sectors, leading to a reduction in unemployment rates.
 
• The other options are not suitable because the acceleration of unemployment means an increase in joblessness, encouragement of unemployment means promoting joblessness, and the addition of unemployment means more people are losing jobs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Acceleration refers to the increase or growth of something, whereas eradication means complete elimination.
 
• Encouragement means providing support or motivation to someone, whereas in this context, it does not apply.
 
• Addition means the act of adding something to increase the quantity or number of things.
 
• However, it is not a suitable option in this context as it does not relate to reducing unemployment rates.

questions.question: Sharad Purnima is associated with the Goddess _______ in some parts of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Lakshmi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Sharad Purnima is a harvest festival celebrated in some parts of India, especially in the northern regions.
 
• This festival is also known as** Kojagiri Purnima and is celebrated on the full moon day of the Hindu lunar month of Ashvin.**
 
• On this day, people worship Goddess Lakshmi, who is believed to bless them with wealth, prosperity, and happiness.
 
• The festival is celebrated with much fervor and enthusiasm, with people lighting lamps, singing and dancing, and preparing special dishes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

** Gauri**

 
• Gauri is another name for Goddess Parvati, who is the consort of Lord Shiva.
 
• She is worshipped as the goddess of fertility, love, and devotion.
 
• However, Sharad Purnima is not specifically associated with Gauri in any part of India.

**Parvati**

 
• Parvati is one of the most popular goddesses in Hindu mythology and is worshipped as the mother goddess.
 
• She is also known as Shakti, the divine feminine energy, and is associated with fertility, power, and strength.
 
• While Sharad Purnima is associated with the goddess Lakshmi, Parvati is also worshipped on this day in some parts of India.

** Sita**

 
• Sita is the wife of Lord Rama and is worshipped as the ideal wife and mother.
 
• She is also known for her devotion and sacrifice, and is considered a symbol of purity and virtue.
 
• However, Sharad Purnima is not specifically associated with Sita in any part of India.

** Lakshmi**

 
• Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth, prosperity, and abundance.
 
• She is worshipped on Sharad Purnima as it is believed that on this day, she visits the earth and blesses her devotees with wealth and happiness.
 
• The festival is also known as Kojagiri Purnima, which means the night when Goddess Lakshmi is worshipped.

questions.question: How many rulers of Dakshinapatha were defeated by Samudragupta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__Samudragupta:__

__
 
• Samudragupta (335-376 AD) was the great ruler of the Gupta dynasty, he was the successor of Chandragupta I.
 
• The most important source of information about the conquests of Samudragupta is the 'Allahabad Pillar' or 'Prayag Prasasti'.
 
• So far the rulers of Dakshinapatha were concerned, Samudragupta maintained a submissive attitude towards them.
 
• There were twelve rulers who surrendered to Samudragupta after being defeated. 
 
• He then allowed all of them to rule again.
 
• On accepting the subjugation of Samudragupta, all the South Indian kings were freed and also offered their daughters in marriage.
 
• They brought tribute, followed his orders, and attended his court.

Samudragupta was a son of the Gupta king Chandragupta I and queen Kumaradevi, who came from a Licchavi family. His fragmentary Eran stone inscription states that his father selected him as the successor because of his "devotion, righteous conduct, and valour".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It mentions that Samudragupta defeated 9 kings in the North, 12 Kings in the South.
 
• Another term used by Harisena for him is Kaviraja.
 
• Samudragupta also assumed the title of Vikramanka.
 
• Samudragupta is also called Napoleon of India.
 
• Samudragupta was the fourth king of the Gupta dynasty and the successor to "Chandragupta-I".
 
• Samudragupta is known as the greatest king of the Gupta dynasty and a valiant warrior and patron of the arts.
 
• Chandragupta-I became king after his father Ghatotkacha (320 AD).
 
• The capital of Samudragupta Gupta's empire was "Pataliputra".
 
• Vishnugupta was the last important ruler of the Gupta dynasty.

questions.question: In badminton singles, at the beginning of the game (0-0) and when the server's score is even, the server serves from which side of the court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Right service court.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **In badminton singles, the server always serves from the right service court when his/her score is even.**
 
• ** When the server's score is odd, he/she serves from the left service court.**
 
• This rule ensures that both players get an** equal chance to serve from both sides of the court.**
 
• The server cannot choose any service court he/she wants to serve from. The service court depends on the server's score.
 
• The server can always serve as long as he/she has not committed a fault or a let.
 
• The server serves from the left service court only when his/her score is odd.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key phrase in the question is "server's score is even." This means that the server has scored 0, 2, 4, 6, etc.
 
• In badminton doubles, the server always serves from the right service court of his/her team's side of the court. When the server's team wins a rally, the same server serves again from the alternate service court.
 
• If the server commits a fault or a let, the opponent becomes the new server and serves from the correct service court based on his/her score.

questions.question:
Although there was a category of industries left to the private sector, the sector was kept under state control through a system of licenses. No new industry was allowed unless a license was obtained from the government.

The above lines are about which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IPR-1956.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The lines mentioned in the statement are about the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 (IPR-1956).**
 
• IPR-1956 was the** third industrial policy of the Indian government that aimed at establishing a socialist pattern of society by reducing private sector participation in industries.**
 
• The policy allowed the private sector to operate in industries that were not included in the** list of industries reserved for the public sector.**
 
• However, the private sector was required to obtain a license from the government to start a new industry.
 
• The licensing system was criticized for promoting corruption, bureaucratic delays, and hindering the growth of the private sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• IPR-1952 was the second industrial policy of the Indian government that aimed at promoting private-sector participation in industries.
 
• IPR-1951 was the first industrial policy of the Indian government that aimed at promoting the development of small-scale industries and village industries.
 
• IPR-1958 was the fourth industrial policy of the Indian government that aimed at promoting the growth of the private sector and reducing state control in industries.

questions.question: Make in India scheme was launched by Government of India in year _______.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The Make in India program aims to convert India to a self-reliant country and to give the Indian economy global recognition.
 
• The Make in India program was started on 25th September 2014.
 
• It was launched by the prime minister of India Narendra Modi.
 
• It was launched during the 12th five-year planning in India.
 
• The Make in India is organized by the government of India.
 
• The main objectives of the Make in India program are:
 
 
• Enforcement of secondary and tertiary sectors in India.
 
• Manufacturing of products in India and sell the products worldwide.
 
• Creating job opportunities for more than 10 million people.
 
• Boosting of India's GDP, trade, and economic growth.

questions.question: What does Part IVA of the Indian Constitutions deal with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Fundamental Duties__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties are defined as the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• These duties set out in Part IV–A of the Constitution, concern individuals and the nation.
 
• The 11 fundamental duties are -
 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect the national flag & National Anthem
 
• Follow ideals of the freedom struggle
 
• Protect sovereignty & integrity of India
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon
 
• Sprit of common brotherhood
 
• Preserve composite culture
 
• Preserve natural environment
 
• Develop scientific temper
 
• Safeguard public property
 
• Strive for excellence
 
• Duty for all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy of India are the guidelines or principles given to the institutes for governing India.

 
 
• They are provided in Part IV (Article 36-51) of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution talks about Fundamental Rights, which are -
 
 
• Right to Equality
 
• Right to freedom
 
• Right against exploitation
 
• Right to freedom of Religion
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• Part V (Articles 52–151) speaks of the executive power of the Union.

questions.question: Which rocks are formed from solidification and cooling of magma?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Igneous rocks.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Igneous rocks are formed from the solidification and cooling of magma.**
 
• Magma is molten rock that is found **beneath the Earth's surface**.
 
• Igneous rocks can be classified into two types - **intrusive and extrusive.**
 
• Intrusive igneous rocks are formed when magma cools slowly beneath the Earth's surface, while extrusive igneous rocks are formed when lava cools quickly on the Earth's surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Chemical sedimentary rocks** are formed from the precipitation of minerals from water, such as halite (rock salt) and gypsum.
 
• **Metamorphic rocks** are formed from the transformation of pre-existing rocks due to heat, pressure, and/or chemical activity.
 
• **Sedimentary rocks** are formed from the accumulation and cementation of sediments, such as sandstone and limestone.
